The ground hums beneath your boots. Somewhere far below, something hums back.
A cold wind off the open plains pulls at your coat. The horizon is broken by the half-buried spires of a city no map admits exists.
A figure watches you from the edge of the firelight. They have not blinked in some time.
Your compass spins, slows, and then points politely behind you.
Three black crows wheel low overhead and bank east, toward a ruin you had not planned to visit.
The mud in the drainage ditch is warmer than the air. It pulses, faintly, like sleep.
A robed pilgrim sits cross-legged in the road, eyes closed, smiling. He does not move as you approach.
The light from your torch falls on a wall that was not there a moment ago.
Somewhere, a bell rings. It is not made of metal.
You realize you have been walking for an hour and have left no footprints.
